ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Fannie Lou Hamer Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing care at the rural community health center for high blood pressure readings, thirst and frequent urination, leg and back aching, and reduced vision in the left eye since an old injury, with consent-based, trauma-informed care and a social needs screen. Concerns: She wants nothing done to her body without being told first what it is and why, and wants the right to say no; She wants to stay well enough to keep working for her community; She worries about the cost of medicines and getting to appointments. [S]

Tobacco: never. Alcohol: none. No drug use [S]

tr.td: Establishing care at the rural community health center for high blood pressure readings, thirst and frequent urination, leg and back aching, and reduced vision in the left eye since an old injury, with consent-based, trauma-informed care and a social needs screen
Two-week review of home blood pressure readings and the repeat urine test, with a kidney ultrasound and a nephrology telehealth consultation from the health center
Six-week review: blood pressure, kidney function and potassium after the new medicines, lipids, retinal photographs, and benefits
Four-month review: A1c, urine albumin, kidney function, mood, social needs, and the metformin dose
Seven-month review: A1c, urine albumin, kidney function, seasonal and age-50 vaccines, screening results, and plans for the winter

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Consent-based, trauma-informed care at every visit: explain each examination, test and procedure beforehand (what it is, why, what it involves, the alternatives, including not doing it), ask her agreement and record it, offer a chaperone or companion of her choosing, let her stop at any time, never perform an unplanned procedure, and keep the plan in writing; written consent for any procedure beyond routine tests

Nephrology consultation by telehealth from the health center, with the community health worker present, for albumin in the urine and reduced kidney function in a woman with an old kidney injury, new diabetes and high blood pressure readings

Blood pressure: a validated home monitor with a large cuff, provided by the health center, with readings twice a day for seven days to confirm the diagnosis; less salt, using foods she can get; recheck in two weeks

Diabetes: metformin extended-release once daily, an A1c every three months until at goal, diabetes self-management education in a group class at the health center, and no medicine that can cause low blood sugar

Kidneys: repeat the urine albumin test, a kidney ultrasound with the consultation, no ibuprofen or naproxen, and kidney function and potassium checks after any blood pressure or kidney medicine is started
Cardiovascular risk: atorvastatin 40 mg with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks, a baseline ECG, and TSH at diagnosis

Eyes and feet: retinal photographs in the clinic, so that no separate trip is needed; a comprehensive foot examination yearly; daily foot checks at home, callus care at the health center and well-fitting shoes

Social needs, with the community health worker: the AHC health-related social needs screen at intake and every few months; help applying for SNAP and the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program; the health center's food pantry and produce program; 211 for other local help; rides arranged for every visit and laboratory test; the sliding-fee scale; 90-day medicine supplies at the discount pharmacy, and phone visits when travel is not possible

Shared decisions and the team: Dr. Batiste-Hill, a nurse, the community health worker and the pharmacist review the plan with her; medicines chosen for cost, once-daily dosing and her preferences; she decides what she accepts
Mood and stress: PHQ-9 at intake and at four months, asked privately; counseling offered at her choice
Vaccines: pneumococcal, hepatitis B and Tdap offered, explained and given only with her agreement; influenza and COVID-19 each autumn

On the consultant's advice: amlodipine 5 mg with benazepril 20 mg in one daily capsule and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily with sick-day rules; potassium and creatinine one to two weeks after starting; urine albumin again at three to four months; blood pressure goal below 130/80; review of kidney treatment by telehealth if albumin stays raised
Laboratory checks on the days she is already at the health center, with a ride arranged in advance for any extra check; home blood draw by the mobile phlebotomy service when no ride can be found
Metformin extended-release increased to 1,500 mg with the evening meal, because the A1c was still above goal
Every examination, test and procedure explained first and done only with her documented agreement, with a chaperone of her choosing, at every visit
Consent documented for every examination, blood draw, ultrasound, photograph, vaccine and screening test; she declined a breast and a pelvic examination, and that was respected
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg in the clinic and at home within six months
A1c below 7% within six to nine months, without low blood sugar
6.9% at seven months; no low blood sugar
Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio lower by at least 30% within six months
88 to 96 mg/g at baseline; 41 mg/g at seven months
Food and utility needs met through benefits, and a dependable way to reach every visit and laboratory test
SNAP and energy assistance in place; rides arranged for every visit after one missed laboratory check; transportation still uncertain on some days
146 to 80 mg/dL on atorvastatin; recheck with the yearly panel
